title: Nine Inches of Opening
subtitle: 胸膛与箱子 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 胸膛与箱子（生活与学习·器物与身体）
meta: 主题语境：胸膛与箱子（生活与学习·器物与身体）　|　核心词汇：chest　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chest 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1945 my mother was sent to open ① chest she could not lift, and she said the opening was the whole of the lesson. The ② chest, meaning the box and not the body, was nine inches deep and was opened by whoever came last; chest, she said, is the only thing in an attic that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ chest in that attic had the same lock, and the ④ chest at the end, meaning the one the family kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever opened properly. Chest, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chest was the whole of the song, meaning the breath it carried and not the box. The ⑥ chest, meaning the breath and not any of that, is the only thing in a song that everybody hears and nobody questions; chest, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a box and a breath. She said the breath is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ chest had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the lock. The ⑧ chest of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine inches and eleven years of opening; chest, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chest I remember is the one at the end, which was opened in 1965 and is still described as the heaviest in the county. A ⑩ chest, my grandmother said in 1970, is the only thing that improves by being opened; every chest, she said, is a breath that has agreed to look like a box. She said the breath was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 箱子（指那只箱子本身，与那副身躯相对）
C. 固定搭配：open a chest 打开一只箱子
D. n. 箱子（指阁楼里每一只）
E. n. 箱子（指末尾那一只）
F. n. 胸腔之气（抽象：它承载的那口气）
G. n. 那口气（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The chest, meaning the box and not the body
chest was the whole of the song
the chest had become a number in a report
The chest of the whole thing
A chest, my grandmother said in 1970

answers.why: open a chest 意为“打开一只箱子”，1945 年母亲被派去打开她抬不动的那只箱子。
chest 意为“箱子、大箱子”，指那只箱子本身而不是那副身躯，深九英寸，由最后来的人打开。
chest 指阁楼里每一只箱子，每一只都是同样的锁。
chest 指末尾那一只（家里保留的那一只），是唯一有人认真打开过的。
chest 意为“胸腔之气”，抽象指它承载的那口气，父亲说 chest 就是那首歌的全部。
chest 为抽象用法，指那口气本身，是一首歌里人人都听见、却没人质疑的东西。
chest 意为“箱子、大箱子”，到 1960 年这只 chest 成了报告里的一个数字。
chest 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英寸和十一年的开启。
chest 意为“箱子”，我记得的是末尾那一只，1965 年打开，至今仍被说成全县最重的。
chest 为抽象总称，祖母说一只箱子是唯一会因为被认真打开而变好的东西。
